text:
kevin: Noticed request-level routing is bouncing between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for the same tenant during the canary. This is causing cache churn and metric noise.
lina: Yep, saw that. Tie-breaker currently uses a nanosecond timestamp + random jitter to avoid hot spots, but that's now causing instability across affinity-sensitive workloads.
prateek: Can we make tie-breaks deterministic per-tenant+request-hash? That would give stickiness without state.
zoe: That helps, but we also rely on the cost model which changes frequently. If cost deltas cause frequent reorders, deterministic tie-break won't stop churn.
kevin: Right. We need a multi-layer approach: (1) stable tie-break seed, (2) cost bucketing (quantize small deltas), (3) soft stickiness TTL for chosen route.
lina: For cost bucketing: bucket by configurable epsilon, e.g., round(latency_ms, 5) and round(unit_cost, 0.0001). Small oscillations won't flip route.
prateek: Soft stickiness: route chosen stays preferred for N requests or T seconds unless severe degradation. We should set defaults like sticky_ttl=60s and max_requests=100.
zoe: Edge case: capacity failures. If the chosen route starts returning 429/503, we should preempt stickiness immediately and failover.
kevin: Agreed. Also want to avoid global state. Implement stickiness as a per-request selection hint stored in KV cache? Or embed sticky metadata in client-side token?
lina: Embedding on client is messy for hosted API. Suggest storing last-chosen route in our fast LRU (tenant->route with TTL). Small memory but effective. We already have shard-local caches.
prateek: Another idea: use exponential backoff for re-evaluations: if a tenant had stable routing, skip full policy re-eval for short interval and reuse previous result unless a trigger (telemetry or config change) occurs.
zoe: Triggers: (a) cost bucket change for top candidate (b) adapter health change (c) explicit control-plane bundle update. Make those events invalidate the sticky entry.
kevin: Telemetry knobs: emit `routing.churn_count`, `routing.sticky_hits`, `routing.re_evals_skipped`. Helps tune default TTLs.
lina: Concern: per-tenant cache can become stale after deployment changes. Ensure control-plane publishes an incrementing policy-bundle-version and the LRU checks it before reusing a cached route.
prateek: Good call. Implementation sketch: cached entry = {route, bundle_version, created_at, perf_bucket}. On eval, if bundle_version != current -> re-eval.
zoe: What about simulation tests? We should fuzz cost noise and simulate thousands of tenants to verify churn reductions.
kevin: Yes. Add a CI job: `routing-stability-sim` that runs candidate policy logic over synthetic latency traces for 1M decisions and reports churn metrics.
lina: One more: tie-break determinism should respect region affinity preferences (authors may prefer locality). So seed = hash(tenant_id + region_priority_list) not just tenant id.
prateek: For cost bucketing semantics, document immutable thresholds vs adaptive ones. Static epsilon is safe; adaptive (percentile-based) is more powerful but riskier. Start static.
zoe: Ops note from infra-bot: infra-bot: routed-caches: memory usage baseline 120MB, projected +20MB with per-tenant sticky LRU. OK for canary but watch growth.
kevin: We should provide a feature flag `routing.sticky_mode=off|soft|strict` to roll out. Soft = buckets + TTL; Strict = pin until explicit invalidation (dangerous).
lina: Also add audit logs for when failovers happen due to health vs cost change. That helps customers debug perceived instability.
prateek: Action items:
 - lina: implement deterministic tie-break seed + bucket rounding PR (ETA 3d)
 - zoe: add sticky LRU with bundle-version checks to runtime cache (ETA 1w)
 - kevin: routing-stability-sim job + baseline run (ETA 1w)
 - infra: monitor memory and add metrics mentioned (ETA 2d)
zoe: Quick config suggestion for canary: `routing.sticky_ttl=30s`, `routing.cost_bucket_ms=5`, `routing.max_adapter_calls_before_reval=1`.
kevin: Sounds good. We'll validate against canary traffic tomorrow. If churn drops >70% we roll to 50% traffic.
lina: Also a doc for policy authors explaining that tiny cost adjustments may not flip routes due to bucketing. Avoid surprises.
prateek: One last thought: some customers want absolute lowest cost even with churn. Consider a per-tenant override `routing.allow_churn=true` that disables stickiness.
zoe: OK. I'll wire that into the LRU lookup.
kevin: Great. If anyone sees weird regressions during canary, call it out here and we'll pause.
